title: General-purpose foundation models surpass specialized ones on chemical property prediction tasks
abstract: arXiv:2610.41899v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Foundation models (FMs) learn reusable representations from large collections of unlabeled data. In chemistry the corresponding data mainly consists of molecular structures, which are abundant, whereas experimental measurements are scarce. Chemical FMs such as ChemBERTa and MoLFormer were therefore trained on diverse molecular structures to enable fine-tuning on small experimental datasets (less than 100 datapoints in most realistic scenarios) and subsequent property prediction. At the same time, general-purpose FMs such as GPT-6 Astra and Claude Opus 5.5 were trained on virtually all publicly available data, including knowledge of the humankind on molecular properties and laws governing them. Here we compare accuracies of chemical and general-purpose FMs on tasks from various areas of chemistry. translated_title: 通用基础模型在化学性质预测任务上超越专用模型
translated_abstract: 基础模型（FMs）从大量未标注数据中学习可复用的表示。在化学领域，相应的数据主要由分子结构组成，这类数据十分丰富，而实验测量数据则较为稀缺。因此，诸如ChemBERTa和MoLFormer等化学基础模型在多样化的分子结构上进行训练，以便能够在小型实验数据集（在大多数现实场景中少于100个数据点）上进行微调并随后进行性质预测。与此同时，诸如GPT-6 Astra和Claude Opus 5.5等通用基础模型几乎在所有公开可用的数据上进行训练，其中包括人类关于分子性质及其规律的知识。在本文中，我们比较了化学基础模型和通用基础模型在化学各领域任务上的准确率。令人惊讶的是，通用的GPT-6 Astra在五项物理化学和量子化学回归任务上超越了目前可用的化学基础模型（摘要在此处截断）。
tldr: 该论文的核心发现是：在化学性质预测任务上，通用基础模型（如GPT-6 Astra）的准确率能够超越专门针对分子结构训练的化学基础模型（如ChemBERTa和MoLFormer）。
en_tdlr: This paper's key finding is that general-purpose foundation models (e.g., GPT-6 Astra) outperform specialized chemical foundation models (e.g., ChemBERTa and MoLFormer) on chemical property prediction tasks.
